note: Temperatures are measurements averaged as f64 and compared with an absolute tolerance (abs() <= 0.05) or ordering (>), never with exact equality.
Cart prices and totals are stored and summed as f64 (unit_price, subtotal, shipping 4.99), i.e. money in floating point.
has_right_angle() compares computed f64 squared distances with ==, so rounding makes the Pythagorean check unreliable for non-integer coordinates.
Money is held as i64 cents (Cents), interest uses integer basis points with integer rounding, and the reconciliation compares integers.

Projectile physics uses f64 for approximate quantities with an integer step counter; landed_at == 0.0 compares against the unset sentinel the code assigned, and the range check uses a 1% relative tolerance.
Tween::keyframes() drives a while loop with a float counter (t += step while t <= 1.0), so the number of frames depends on accumulated rounding.
Payroll amounts (hourly_rate 18.35, gross, tax, net, team totals) are computed and accumulated as f64, i.e. money in floating point.
Sensor statistics are approximate measurements; merged and direct results are compared with a relative tolerance via approx_eq and swing with >, and map keys and counters are integers.
Bank balances, fees and holdings are f64 money, and main checks opening_total == closing_total with exact float equality on summed values.
Ray/shape geometry uses f64 with an EPS tolerance for degeneracy and hit tests, total_cmp to pick the nearest hit, and a tolerance for the area check; no money or exact equality.
